D5 — When a webhook delivery fails, should we retry it (at-least-once) or keep the current at-most-once guarantee?

questions.question:
D7 — Should the backoff curve add jitter (randomized delay) or stay deterministic?
Project/branch/task: main branch; PLAN.md retry framework, Architecture (custom backoff function approved in D4).
ELI10: If a downstream service blips for a second, hundreds of jobs fail at the same moment. With a deterministic curve they all retry at exactly the same moment too, hit the recovering service together, fail together, and repeat. Jitter spreads each job's retry randomly inside its window so the retries trickle in instead of stampeding.
Stakes if we pick wrong: without jitter a short outage turns into a self-inflicted repeating spike; the downstream service sees a wave every 2s, 4s, 8s and may never recover.
Recommendation: A because full jitter is one line inside the backoff function and it is the standard recommendation from AWS, Google Cloud and every resilience library (human: ~30 min / CC: ~2 min).
Completeness: A=10/10, B=6/10
Net: predictable timestamps (B) versus not re-creating the outage you are recovering from (A).

options.label: A) Full jitter (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Retries after a shared outage spread across the window; no synchronized retry storm. ✅ One line in the backoff function; the library still owns scheduling, so nothing else changes. ❌ Retry timing is no longer exactly predictable; tests must assert bounds, not exact delays.

options.description: ✅ Exact, predictable delays make log timelines easy to read. ✅ Simplest possible test: assert the exact delay per attempt. ❌ Every job that failed together retries together; the classic thundering-herd footgun documented in the search sources.

questions.question:
D13 — Should the dependency graph be computed once and cached with the job, or recomputed from a fresh payload fetch on every retry?
Project/branch/task: main branch; PLAN.md retry framework, Performance section.
ELI10: Each retry currently re-downloads the whole job payload from the database and rebuilds the dependency graph from scratch, even though nothing about the job changed since the last attempt. With up to 8 attempts, that is 8 fetches and 8 rebuilds per failing job, and during an outage every job is failing at once, so the database gets hammered exactly when the system is already unhealthy. Caching the graph on the first attempt makes retries cheap.
Stakes if we pick wrong: caching a graph that should have been rebuilt (payload changed) retries with stale dependencies; not caching turns a downstream outage into a database load spike of our own making.
Recommendation: A because the retry window is 10 minutes and the payload is immutable for a queued job in every standard library, so the cache is safe; guard it with a payload version check so a mutable payload still invalidates (human: ~half day / CC: ~10 min).
Completeness: A=9/10, B=5/10, C=n/a (measurement only, decides nothing)
Net: a small cache with an invalidation guard (A) versus paying the full cost on every attempt when the system is already stressed (B).

options.label: A) Cache the graph on attempt 1, load-only on retries, invalidate on payload version change (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Retries cost one small read instead of a full payload fetch plus graph rebuild; DB load during outages stays flat. ✅ Version check keeps correctness if a payload is ever edited between attempts. ❌ Needs somewhere to store the serialized graph (job metadata or a column) and a test for the invalidation path.

options.label: B) Refetch and recompute every attempt, as planned
options.description: ✅ Always operates on the freshest payload; no invalidation logic to get wrong. ✅ Zero new storage. ❌ Up to 8x the fetch and compute cost per failing job, concentrated during outages when the DB is least able to absorb it.

options.label: C) Measure first inside the integration test, decide after
options.description: ✅ Replaces a 7/10 confidence estimate with real numbers. ✅ Cheap: the D12 integration test already runs the retry loop; add timing. ❌ Leaves R5 open; the plan ships without a decision on the retry hot path.
